props.title: Every Little Step

sections.content: Every Little Step brilliantly captures the meta-theatrical nature of Broadway casting by documenting the audition process for the 2006 revival of A Chorus Line (1975). The documentary's genius lies in how it mirrors the very show it's about - both tell stories of dancers desperately trying to land roles in a musical. The parallel between the real-life dancers and the characters they're auditioning to play creates an fascinating recursive loop, especially since A Chorus Line itself was based on real dancers' taped conversations from the 1970s. This documentary stands alongside other great performing arts films like The Company (2003) and Ballet 422 (2014) in revealing the intense physical and emotional demands of professional dance.

sections.content: The raw vulnerability captured in Every Little Step connects deeply to other documentaries about the brutally competitive nature of performing arts. First Position (2011) follows young ballet competitors with similar dreams, while Showbusiness: The Road to Broadway (2007) expands the scope to show the entire ecosystem of mounting Broadway productions. The film's intimate portrayal of rejection and resilience particularly resonates with Casting By (2012), which examines how split-second decisions in audition rooms can change performers' lives forever.

What makes Every Little Step especially powerful is its exploration of the cyclical nature of theater history. The original A Chorus Line revolutionized Broadway by putting dancers' real stories center stage. Watching new performers audition for these roles 30 years later demonstrates how universal these experiences remain. This connects to other theatrical documentaries like Moon Over Broadway (1997) and Broadway: The Golden Age (2003) in preserving crucial moments in theater history. sections.content: The documentary gains additional weight by capturing original A Chorus Line creators like Baayork Lee passing the torch to a new generation. This preservation of theatrical legacy recalls Original Cast Album: Company (1970) and Best Worst Thing That Ever Could Have Happened (2016), both of which document pivotal moments in musical theater history. The film shows how A Chorus Line's revolutionary approach to storytelling continues influencing contemporary theater, as seen in shows like Hamilton (2015) and A Strange Loop (2019).
